scenes.heading: Units and converting
scenes.say: Is three metres the same as three hundred centimetres? Yes! In this video you'll learn how to switch between metric units without getting mixed up.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: One $10 note = ten $1 coins: more pieces, same value
scenes.science: 1 m = 100 cm: smaller unit, bigger number, same length
scenes.breaks: Money swaps use many amounts like 5, 20 and 50. Metric units only jump by 10, 100 or 1000.
scenes.say: Think about money. One ten dollar note is worth the same as ten one dollar coins. Swap to smaller coins and you hold more pieces. Units work the same way. Change to a smaller unit and the number gets bigger, but the length stays the same.

scenes.heading: The facts to know
scenes.say: Here are the facts to learn. One centimetre is ten millimetres. One metre is one hundred centimetres. One kilometre is one thousand metres. One kilogram is one thousand grams, and one tonne is one thousand kilograms. One litre is one thousand millilitres.
scenes.caption: 1 cm = 10 mm. 1 m = 100 cm. 1 km = 1000 m. 1 kg = 1000 g, and 1 t = 1000 kg. 1 L = 1000 mL.

scenes.heading: Multiply or divide?
scenes.say: Here's the rule. Going from a big unit to a small unit, multiply. Going from a small unit to a big unit, divide.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Convert 2750 g to kilograms.
lines: g → kg: small to big, so divide
scenes.say: Convert two thousand seven hundred and fifty grams to kilograms. Grams to kilograms is small unit to big unit, so divide. There are one thousand grams in a kilogram. Two thousand seven hundred and fifty divided by one thousand is two point seven five kilograms.
scenes.caption: Convert 2750 g to kilograms. Small unit to big unit, so divide. 1 kg = 1000 g. 2750 ÷ 1000 = 2.75 kg.

scenes.heading: Adding mixed units
scenes.question: Add 1.4 m, 85 cm and 600 mm. Give the answer in metres.
scenes.say: Now add one point four metres, eighty-five centimetres and six hundred millimetres. First change everything to centimetres: one hundred and forty, eighty-five and sixty. Add them to get two hundred and eighty-five centimetres. Divide by one hundred: two point eight five metres.
scenes.caption: Add 1.4 m, 85 cm and 600 mm. Change everything to cm: 140, 85 and 60. Add to get 285 cm. Divide by 100: 2.85 m.

scenes.say: Quick recap. A smaller unit means a bigger number. Big to small, multiply. Small to big, divide. And always change to the same unit before you add or compare. Now try the practice questions!
